caesar.name: Caesar
caesar.description: Shifts each letter by a fixed number of positions in the alphabet.
caesar.principle: Each letter is replaced by the one located k positions further, wrapping from Z back to A: C = (P + k) mod 26.

substitution.name: Substitution
substitution.description: Replaces each letter with another according to a shuffled alphabet.
substitution.principle: A 26-letter substitution alphabet, often built from a keyword, maps each plaintext letter to a unique ciphertext letter.

permutation.name: Permutation
permutation.principle: The text is split into blocks, padded with X if needed. Within each block, positions are shuffled according to a permutation: the letters stay the same, only their positions change.

vigenere.name: Vigenère
vigenere.description: Applies a different Caesar shift to each letter, based on a repeating key.
vigenere.principle: The key is repeated over the entire length of the message and each letter is shifted by the value of the corresponding key letter: Ci = (Pi + Ki) mod 26.
